panels.rationale: The radiograph demonstrates widening of the ulnar aspect of the first MCP joint, which the article identifies as consistent with a Pseudo-Stener lesion due to proximal ulnar collateral ligament rupture. This falls under the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Lerman et al. Pseudo-Stener lesion due to proximal ulnar collateral ligament rupture: A case report.. International journal of surgery case reports 2023. doi:10.1016/j.ijscr.2023.108141. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
in_text_mentions: X-Ray imaging from an outside facility (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3) demonstrated widening of the ulnar aspect of the 1st MCP joint in non-stress views. There were no bony avulsions, fractures, or dislocations. Based on patient history and compelling physical exam findings, the patient was diagnosed with a right thumb MCP UCL rupture. Patient elected to undergo operative intervention with thumb UCL Repair.Fig. 1Radiographic image of hand.Fig. 1Fig. 2Radiographic image of hand.Fig. 2Fig. 3Radiographic image of hand.Fig. 3

panels.rationale: The image provides a coronal T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI of the thumb demonstrating the ulnar collateral ligament subluxated ulnar to the adductor aponeurosis, which is the radiological definition of a Stener lesion, a specific mechanism of thumb ulnar collateral ligament injury.
